sections.title: Agreement and placement of adjectives (BAGS rule)

grammar_rules.title: Adjective agreement in gender and number
grammar_rules.summary: Adjectives agree in gender (+e for fem) and number (+s for plural) with the noun they modify.
grammar_rules.explanation:
Special masculine forms before vowel/silent h: beau -> bel, nouveau -> nouvel, vieux -> vieil.
Feminine forms: belle, nouvelle, vieille.
exceptions: Compound color adjectives (bleu marine, vert clair) and invariable colors (marron, orange) do not agree.

common_mistakes.explanation: Use bel before masculine noun starting with vowel.

grammar_rules.title: Placement of adjectives: the BAGS rule (Beauty, Age, Goodness, Size)
grammar_rules.summary: Most adjectives follow the noun in French, except BAGS adjectives which precede the noun.
grammar_rules.explanation:
- Beauty: beau, joli
- Age: jeune, vieux, nouveau
- Goodness: bon, mauvais, meilleur, gentil
- Size: grand, petit, gros, haut, long
Example: 'une jolie maison', 'un vieux livre', 'une grande ville'.
notes: Some adjectives change meaning based on position: grand homme (great man) vs homme grand (tall man); pauvre homme (pitiful) vs homme pauvre (poor).

questions.prompt: Patrick est doué. Sonia est . Comparatives and superlatives Comparison of adjectives and adverbs In French, comparisons of adjectives and adverbs can take three forms, plus... que (more . . . than), moins... que (less . . . than), aussi... que (as . . . as). For example: Ce modèle est plus récent que le mien. This model is more recent than mine. New York est plus grand que San Francisco. New York is bigger than San Francisco. Marc est moins riche que Paul. Mark is less rich than Paul. Luc est aussi célèbre que Bertrand. Luc is as famous as Bertrand. Comparison of nouns To compare quantities, use the following expressions. Note the use of de (d') with expressions of quantity: Elle a plus de temps que Valérie. She has more time than Valérie. Il a moins de chance que toi. He is less lucky than you are. Elle a autant de jouets que toi. She has as many toys as you do. Irregular comparatives Some comparatives have irregular forms. Ce livre est bon. This book is good. Ce livre-ci est meilleur que ce livre-là. This book is better than that book. Il se porte bien. He's feeling well. Il se porte mieux qu'avant. He is feeling better than before. La situation économique est mauvaise. The economic situation is bad. La situation économique est pire qu'avant. The economic situation is worse than before. Cela n'a pas le moindre intérêt. That does not have the slightest interest. Superlatives To express the ideas of the most, the least, the best, the worst, etc., one uses the superlative. To form the superlative in French, simply precede the comparative form by the definite article. Note that before naming a group or entity, the superlative is followed by de  the definite article. 188 practice makes perfect Complete French Grammar C'est le plus grand spectacle du monde. It's the greatest show on earth. C'est la plus belle histoire que j'aie jamais lue. It's the most beautiful story I ever read. C'est l'endroit le moins ennuyeux de toute It's the least boring place in the whole city. la ville. The irregular adjectives you learned with the comparatives are also used in the superlative. Ce roman est bon. This novel is good. C'est son meilleur roman. It's his best novel. C'est un mauvais cauchemar. It's a bad nightmare. C'est son pire cauchemar. It's his worst nightmare.
